newsitem.title: UK: Stg strength means UK rate rise not needed - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Stg strength means UK rate rise not needed - CBI.

text.p: Sterling's strong rally means a UK rate rise is not needed in the first half if this year, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday.

"Our forecasting judgement is that rates can remain at this level, six percent, in the first half of this year, and that is because inflationary pressures are subdued - the rise in the pound has been a dampening pressure," Sudhir Junankar, CBI's associate director of economic analysis told RFTV in an interview.
He said looking further out, domestic demand is reasonably robust and some inflationary pressure may emerge.
"So the forecasting judgement we have made is that perhaps a half point rise in base rates is required in the second half of this year and perhaps another half point in early 1998."
